### The Clock's Long Shadow

Long before [DST]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="DST abbr. daylight saving time 经济时"} was invented to squeeze an extra hour of light from the reluctant sun, people read time in simpler contrasts: [dawn]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dawn · n. 拂晓，破晓，黎明; 开端；曙光；萌芽; 破晓；开始; 见分晓，水落石出；变得明朗 Dawnn. 道恩"}, when the sky cracked pale and cold over the fields, and [dusk]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dusk · n. 黄昏，薄暮；幽暗，昏暗; 微暗的; 使变微暗; 变微暗"}, when the same fields dissolved into shadow. Between those two poles, the day ran its [cycle]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cycle · n. 循环；周期；整套；自行车；一段时间; 使循环；使轮转; 骑自行车；循环；轮转"} — not always tidily, not always on schedule, but always forward.

Civilizations, too, moved in cycles. Each [epoch]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="epoch · n. 纪元, 时期, 时代"} announced its own [advent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="advent · n. 出现, 到来"} with fanfare, then quietly began to [decay]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="decay · vi. 腐烂，腐朽；衰退，衰减; 衰退，衰减；腐烂，腐朽; 使腐烂，使腐败；使衰退，使衰落"}. What an [eon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="eon · n. 永世；无数的年代；极长时期"} of geology accomplishes in stone, a century of politics manages in the reputations of empires. Power was in [flux]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="flux · n. 连续的改变；不稳定的状态"}: it rose, peaked, and entered its [ebb]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ebb · n. 退潮；衰退；衰落; 衰退；衰落；潮退；减少 EBBabbr. Early Basic Breccia…"} before anyone had quite noticed the turn. And what [ensued]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ensue · vi. 跟着发生，接着发生；继起; 追求"} was rarely the clean break the victors promised — more often a long [hiatus]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hiatus · n. 裂缝，空隙；脱漏部分"}, a gap in the record, a silence that only later generations could read as transition.

Progress was seldom free of [lag]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lag · n. 迟延；防护套；囚犯；桶板；落后; 押往监狱；落后于；加上外套; 滞后；缓缓而行；蹒跚; 最后的"}. Ideas that would one day remake the world spent [prior]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="prior · adj. 在先的，在前的；优先的; 在前，居先 Prior普赖尔"} decades ignored, their champions dismissed as [tardy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tardy · adj. 行动缓慢的, 缓缓移动的, 迟缓的; 晚的, 迟的"} arrivals to conversations that had not yet started. A thinker might endure a lonely [stint]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stint · n. 节约；定额，定量；从事某项工作的时间；有限供给，有限的努力；滨鹬；一段时间 节省；限制；节约，吝啬；…"} at the margins before the age finally [morphed]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="morph · n. 词态；语素；变体; 在屏幕上变换图像；改变"} around their insight. Change did not announce itself; it accumulated. One [nonce]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="nonce · n. 现时,目前"} observation became a pattern; a pattern **begot** a theory; the theory, once it [ceased]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ceased · v. 中止；中断；停止"} to be controversial, hardened into common sense and eventually into [relic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="relic · n. 遗物, 遗迹, 遗产; 遗体, 尸骸"}.

In the [midst]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="midst · n. 当中，中间; 在…中间"} of it all, individuals felt only the grain of the immediate: the [haste]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="haste · n. 匆忙；急忙；轻率; 匆忙；赶紧; 赶快"} with which a deadline approached, the need to [hurry]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hurry · vt. &amp; 催促；急忙; 匆忙，急忙"} a decision before circumstance decided for them, the way a good season could [elapse]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="elapse · vi. 时间过去；消逝; 时间的过去；流逝"} before one had properly enjoyed it. Those who learned to [forego]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="forego · vt. 走在…之前,居先"} urgency — to let time work on a problem — often found that what looked like the [demise]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="demise · n. 死亡，终止；转让；传位; 遗赠；禅让"} of a plan was merely its dormancy. The thing would [recur]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="recur · vi. 重现；复发；再来；采用；循环；递归"}, altered and stronger. It always did. Whatever came before had not been wasted; it had simply been [altering]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="alter · vt. 改变，更改; 改变；修改"} itself, grain by grain, into whatever came next.

### The Clock That Cannot Be Rewound

At the [outset]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="outset · n. 开始, 开端"}, the old [sundial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sundial · n. 日晷, 日规"} stood in the garden like a patient teacher, its shadow [ticking]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ticking · n. 坚质条纹棉布或亚麻布；滴答响声"} across stone as the morning light climbed. The village was [nascent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="nascent · adj. 初期的；新生的；萌芽的；未成熟的"} then — a [budding]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="budding · adj. 正发芽的；开始发育的,成长中的; 新获得成功的,初露头角的; 发芽"} cluster of rooftops and mud lanes where every [grownup]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="grownup · n. 成年人; 已长成的"} still remembered the smell of [infancy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="infancy · n. 婴儿期；幼年；初期"}, and the young had not yet learned that time moves in only one direction.

Those early decades felt [cyclical]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cyclical · adj. 周期的，循环的"}, the seasons **preceding** each other with a kind of comfort. In the long [interim]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="interim · adj. 临时的，暂时的；中间的；间歇的; 过渡时期，中间时期；暂定"} between harvests, life seemed to enter a [dormant]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dormant · adj. 潜伏的,蛰服的,休眠的"} [stasis]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stasis · n. 郁积，停滞；血行停滞"} — fields resting, ambitions quietly [slumbering]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="slumber · n. 睡眠；麻木状态；静止状态; 睡眠；蛰伏；麻木; 睡眠；睡着度过"} in the cold. Yet beneath that stillness the world was already shifting. Fortunes began to [crumble]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="crumble · vt. &amp; 弄碎, 碎成细屑; 衰落, 崩溃"} and [dwindle]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dwindle · vi. 逐渐变少或变小"}; old certainties that once felt [mature]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mature · adj. 成熟的；到期的；成年人的；充分考虑的; 到期；成熟; 使…成熟；使…长成；慎重作出"} and solid turned brittle. Anxiety [loomed]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="looming · n. 上现蜃景；庞视；幽影; 隐隐约约的；正在逼近的; 逼近；隐约可见"} on the horizon long before anyone named it, and the [lagging]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lagging · n. 绝缘层材料; 落后的"} signs of decay were easy to miss when you were busy tending to [recess]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="recess · n. 中止或暂停期间; 学校的课间休息; 壁凹；壁龛; 某物内部的凹形空间; 遥远或隐秘的地方; 把某物放…"} and routine.

The hardest lesson was that you cannot [rewind]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="rewind · n. 重绕；倒带器; 重绕；倒回; 倒回；重绕"} the tape. What the [bygones]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bygones · n. 往事；往昔恩怨"} held — the laughter, the quarrels, the long afternoons when light would [linger]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="linger · vi. 逗留, 徘徊; 缓慢消失"} on the water — could only be [relived]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="relive · vt. 再体验; 复活；再生"} in memory, never in fact. Grief, if left alone, tends to [regress]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="regress · vi. 退化, 退步, 倒退"} into numbness; but numbness, too, will eventually [subside]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="subside · vi. 平息；沉淀；减弱；坐下"} if you do not let sorrow [retard]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="retard · vt. 使减速；妨碍；阻止; 推迟，延迟; 使延迟; 减慢；受到阻滞; 减速；阻滞；延迟"} the slow work of healing. Some mornings a person must simply [commence]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="commence · vt. 开始；着手; 使……开始；使……得学位"} again: let the old aches [perish]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="perish · vt. 使麻木；毁坏; 死亡；毁灭；腐烂；枯萎"}, refuse to let the fear of what is [looming]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="looming · n. 上现蜃景；庞视；幽影; 隐隐约约的；正在逼近的; 逼近；隐约可见"} become an excuse for [stasis]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stasis · n. 郁积，停滞；血行停滞"}. At **last**, the [kickoff]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="kickoff · n. 开始；开球"} of a new chapter rarely announces itself with fanfare — it arrives quietly, the way dawn does, and you only recognize it looking back.

### The Long Arc of a River Valley

[Prior to]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="prior to 在...之前"} the age of maps, people read time through the land itself. In the [forenoon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="forenoon · n. 上午；午前"}, when mist still clung to the ridgeline, elders would point to the layered cliffs and speak of [antiquity]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="antiquity · n. 古老；年代久远；；古代; 古迹，古物; 古代的风俗习惯; 古人们"} — of a world so old that the [Jurassic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Jurassic · adj. 侏罗纪的；侏罗系的; 侏罗纪"} strata beneath their feet had once been seabed. Nothing about that deep past felt [ephemeral]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ephemeral · adj. 短暂的,瞬息的"}; it pressed against the present like stone.

Yet change is never still. Rivers [stagnate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stagnate · vi. 停滞, 不流动, 不发展"} only in drought; the rest of the year they cut and carve, and the valley records each [upheaval]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="upheaval · n. 剧变；隆起；举起"} in silt and scar. [Hitherto]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hitherto · adv. 到目前为止"} the floodplain had held its shape, but the spring thaw brought a [reversal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="reversal · n. 逆转；撤销；反转"} — channels jumped their banks, old sandbars [perished]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="perished · adj. 感觉很冷的；脆裂的; 枯萎；灭亡"}, and [emerging]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="emerging · adj. 新兴的；出现的；形成的; 形成；浮现；由…中脱出；显露"} islands rearranged the whole lower reach. Farmers watched the [climactic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="climactic · adj. 高潮的;形成高潮的"} surge and then the slow [cessation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cessation · n. 停止,休止,中断"} of the waters, knowing the [aftermath]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="aftermath · n. 后果"} would demand new seed-lines, new fences. Progress is rarely steady; it comes [fitfully]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="fitfully · adv. 断断续续地；发作地"}, [alternate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="alternate · adj. 轮流的, 交替的; 间隔的; 代替的; &amp; 交替, 轮换"} seasons of loss and [flourish]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="flourish · v. 繁荣；昌盛；兴旺; 茁壮成长；健康幸福; 挥舞; 夸张动作; 给人深刻印象的行动；令人难忘的方式; …"}.

By midsummer the valley had reached a kind of [maturity]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="maturity · n. 成熟;成熟期;发育完全; 到期"}. The river ran clear, grasses achieved an [enduring]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="enduring · adj. 持久的,不朽的"} green, and children played on banks that had looked [imminent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="imminent · adj. 迫近的；即将来临的"}ly dangerous only weeks before. But the calendar pressed on regardless. A [countdown]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="countdown · n. 倒数读秒,倒计时; 大事临近的时期"} had already begun in the thinning light — the [temporal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="temporal · adj. 时间的; 暂存的，短暂的，非永恒的; 世俗的；现世的; 表示时间的，"} window before first frost was shorter than it felt. Elders sensed the [exigency]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="exigency · n. 紧急；紧急事件"} and moved to [expedite]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="expedite · vt. 加快进展; 迅速完成"} the harvest, unwilling to let abundance [intermit]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="intermit · v. 中断"} into waste. They scheduled no [downtime]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="downtime · n. 停工时间，停止运行时间; 停机时间; 停工时间；休息时间"} until the grain was in.

What the valley taught was the [emergence]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="emergence · n. 出来;现出;出现;暴露"} of pattern from apparent chaos: a [fleeting]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="fleeting · adj. 飞逝的；转瞬间的; 迅速移动"} flood becomes the foundation of next year's soil; a [cessation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cessation · n. 停止,休止,中断"} of growth precedes the deepest root-work; even the [obituary]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="obituary · adj. 死亡的；讣告的; 讣告"} of a season is a prologue. Resting in that knowledge, the people accepted the rhythm — not as surrender to [eternity]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="eternity · n. 来世，来生；不朽；永世"}, but as literacy in time itself.

### When the Sandglass Runs Low

[Antecedent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="antecedent · n. 发生在前的事，先例; 先行词; 前项; 前件; 经历；学历; 祖先; 前身; 在前的，在先的，先行的"} civilizations understood time not as a line but as a wheel. They watched the [solstices]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="solstices 二至点"} mark the sky's turning points, and [forthwith]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="forthwith · adv. 即刻,毫不拖延地"} built stone calendars to honour each shift. The [sandglass]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sandglass · n. 沙漏"} was their intimate companion — a quiet, [recurring]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="recurring"} witness to how moments slipped away. In those [primaeval]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="primaeval · adj. 原始的"} ages, change moved on a vast [timescale]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="timescale 时间表,时标,时间量程"}, and yet even the most [eventless]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="eventless · adj. 平静无事的,平静的,平凡的"} stretches of pastoral life were [indelibly]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="indelibly · adv. 不能消灭地"} scored by the seasons. Nothing stayed [suspended]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="suspended · adj. 暂停的，缓期的；悬浮的"} for long; even the stillest valley was [eternally]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="eternally · adv. 永恒地;常常;不绝地"} in motion beneath its surface.

Then came the centuries that [transformed]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="transform · vt. &amp; 改变"} everything. The [preceding]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="preceding · adj. 在先的, 在前的, 前面的"} order — slow, ceremonial, tied to the solstice fire — began to [phase out]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="phase out 逐渐停止；使逐步淘汰"} as new rhythms took hold. Each [milestone]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="milestone · n. 重要事件;重要阶段;转折点;里程碑"} arrived as a [precursor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="precursor · n. 先驱；先行者；先兆，前兆; 初期形式"} to the next upheaval, and historians would later remark, with the benefit of [hindsight]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hindsight · n. 事后的觉悟;事后的聪明"}, that every decisive shift had its [opportune]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="opportune · adj. 合适的，恰好的；及时的，适时的; 恰好地，适时地; 恰好，适时，及时"} moment, a brief and [transient]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="transient · adj. 短暂的，转瞬即逝的；暂时的; 暂住者；流动人口"} window in which the old could be [supersede]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="supersede · vt. 取代, 接替"}d before it calcified again. What [transpired]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="transpire · vi. 发生；蒸发；泄露 使蒸发；使排出"} across each [trimester]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="trimester · n. 三个月,学期"} of a century might only become legible in the [follow-up]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="follow-up · adj. 继续的,作为重复的"} generations who inherited the wreckage and the gifts alike.

The hardest lessons concern [prolonged]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="prolonged · adj. 持续很久的,长时间的"} waiting. A [lingering]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lingering · adj. 拖延的;逗留不去的"} illness, a [sustained]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sustained · adj. 持久的;持续的"} grief, a [premortal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="premortal · adj. 死前的"} stillness — these stretch a person across time in ways that no calendar can measure. [Hereafter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hereafter · adv. 今后,从此以后"}, wrote one forgotten essayist, the [tardiness]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tardiness · n. 缓慢"} of healing should not be mistaken for failure; slow change is still change. [Whereupon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="whereupon · conj. 在这以后, 然后, 于是"} he closed his journal, set down his pen, and let the [sandglass]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sandglass · n. 沙漏"} run.

### When a Century Becomes a Breath

In [retrospect]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="retrospect · n. 回顾，追溯; 回顾，追溯；回想，追忆"}, every great civilization appears to have followed the same arc. What begins as a [primordial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="primordial · adj. 初生的,初发的,原始的"} stirring — a handful of people trading ideas across a fire — grows into something vast and bewildering. A [burgeoning]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="burgeoning · adj. 迅速成长的; 迅速发展的"} settlement becomes a city; a city becomes an empire; and before the [centennial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="centennial · n. 一百周年"} torch is even lit, the founders are already [posthumous]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="posthumous · adj. 死后发生的；死后获得的; 作者死后出版的; 死后出生的，遗腹的"} figures, their names carved in stone rather than spoken aloud. Each [predecessor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="predecessor · n. 前任, 前辈; 原有事物, 前身"} believed their own age to be the [culmination]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="culmination · n. 顶点；高潮"} of all that came before, never suspecting they occupied merely the [penultimate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="penultimate · adj. 倒数第二的"} chapter of a far longer story.

Change never [take place]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="take place 发生；举行"} at a single moment — it unfolds across [successive]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="successive · adj. 连续的, 相继的"} waves, each [intervening]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="intervening · adj. 发生于其间的"} generation inheriting a world slightly altered from the one before. Some shifts are [transitory]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="transitory · adj. 不持续的; 短暂的,转瞬即逝的"}, lasting no longer than a [nanosecond]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="nanosecond · n. 十亿分之一秒"} in historical time; others [perpetuate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="perpetuate · vt. 使永存；使人记住不忘"} themselves across a [millennial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="millennial · adj. 一千年的,千福年的"} span, reshaping the very vocabulary we use to think. What [chronically]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="chronically · adv. 慢性地,习惯性地,长期地"} ails a society — the slow [degenerate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="degenerate · vi. 衰退；堕落；退化; 衰退的，堕落的"} erosion of trust, the [alternating]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="alternating · adj. 交互的; 交替的"} bursts of reform and reaction — rarely announces itself. It accumulates quietly, the way a river carves a canyon: invisible until the canyon is there.

A [provisional]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="provisional · adj. 暂时的;临时的"} truce is signed, and a [transition]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="transition · n. 过渡; 转变; 变迁 (从某一状态或活动）转变，过度"} begins. Planners draw up [preliminary]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="preliminary · adj. 初步的, 预备的, 开端的; 准备工作, 初步行动"} blueprints for a new order. A [centenarian]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="centenarian · adj. 百岁或逾百岁以上的；百岁老人"} who lived through the [millennium]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="millennium · n. 一千年，千年期；千禧年，全人类未来的幸福时代，太平盛世 Millennium白蜜，大白圆粒"}'s turn watches from her window as her grandchildren move at speeds she cannot follow, acting [prematurely]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="prematurely · adv. 过早地;贸然地"} on hopes that have not yet ripened. The city throws a festival to [commemorate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="commemorate · vt. 纪念, 庆祝"} its founding — [prime time]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="prime time · n. 黄金时间"} broadcast, lights everywhere — promising that the memory will be kept in [perpetuity]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="perpetuity · n. 永久;永恒;永远; 永远；永久"}. But the [recurrence]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="recurrence · n. 复发;反复;重现"} of history is its own quiet irony: [millennial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="millennial · adj. 一千年的,千福年的"} promises, [prehistoric]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="prehistoric · adj. 史前的；有文字记载以前的；远古的; 古旧不堪的，完全过时的，陈腐的"} fears, and the [succession]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="succession · n. 连续; 连续不断的人; 继承，继任；继承权"} of dawns that neither confirms nor denies either.

### When Time Folds Back on Itself

The geologist spread her notes across the table, arranging them in [chronological]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="chronological · adj. 按时间的前后顺序排列的; 按时间的前后顺序排列地"} order — oldest strata at the left, youngest at the right. Her life's work was the [Mesozoic Era]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mesozoic era 中生代"}, that vast corridor of deep time when dinosaurs ruled and the continents still drifted in slow, [successional]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="successional · adj. 接连的,连续性的"} waves of collision and rifting. She had spent thirty years tracing the [vicissitudes]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="vicissitudes · n. 变迁,世事变化"} of climate locked inside limestone and shale, each layer a frozen moment in a process that [revolutionized]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="revolutionize · vt. 使彻底变革"} our understanding of how life adapts to change.

Her research, [coincidentally]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="coincidentally · adv. 巧合地, 同时发生"}, had been published the same week as a major [commemoration]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="commemoration · n. 纪念;纪念仪式"} at the university — a century since the founding of the geology department. At the ceremony, a colleague delivered a [retrospective]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="retrospective · adj. 回顾的; 有追溯效力的"} lecture on how plate tectonics had, [simultaneously]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="simultaneously · adv. 同时地"}, unsettled and unified three separate fields of science. The [synchronization]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="synchronization · n. 同一时刻;同步"} of those intellectual revolutions, he argued, was no accident; paradigm shifts tend to cluster. The audience laughed when he admitted that he had nearly missed his own talk, having [procrastinated]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="procrastinate · vi. 拖延,耽搁"} all week on finishing his slides — [procrastination]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="procrastination · n. 延迟,拖延"}, he quipped, being one human habit that no amount of geological time seems to cure.

Outside, rain fell in [intermittent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="intermittent · adj. 间歇的; 断断续续的"} bursts, drumming the courtyard in fits and starts. A junior researcher lingered by the door, watching it. She was the department's youngest hire, beginning what might become a [cradle-to-grave]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cradle-to-grave · adj. 一辈子的,一生的"} devotion to the same ancient rock record her mentor had given her life to. She had already learned to [put something off]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Put something Off."} when the evidence was incomplete rather than rush to conclusions. And she was learning, too, the quieter lesson the geologist's career embodied: that [in hindsight]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="In hindsight thought."}, the slowest processes — erosion, drift, the patient turning of epochs — are always the ones that change everything.
